messages:
mike: Heads up — v2 cutover scheduled for 03/22 02:00 UTC. Quick blocker: saw a header quirk in staging that could misroute a handful of tenants. posting logs/snippet.

deploybot: Reminder: automatic canary will run at cutover. Use /deploybot pin-tenant <tenant> to pin to v1 if needed.

alex: what's the quirk?

mike: Some mobile SDKs send two different version headers (different casing/order). Gateway currently treats headers case-sensitively and picks the first header seen. Example from staging:

```
X-API-Version: 2
Api-Version: v1
User-Agent: RedwoodMobile/1.2.3
```

When the client sends `Api-Version: v1` first, the request routes to v1 despite the SDK including the new header. Means post-cutover some clients may end up on v1 unexpectedly.

jen: can we just normalize headers at the gateway (casefold + canonicalize) before routing? Seems straightforward.

sara: agree, normalization is correct long-term. small patch but needs canary/testing. timeline?

alex: patch is ~30m to implement + canary. We can push as a small config change to the gateway cluster but it needs to be staged in edge-canary first.

mike: given cutover tight window, two options: 1) deploy gateway normalization before cutover (risk small config change in path); 2) pin affected tenants to v1 for 24h and unpin after we roll normalization or confirm no issues. I prefer pin for immediate safety.

jen: OK. Which tenants are affected?

mike: telemetry shows skew for these tenant ids: tenant-a, tenant-b, tenant-kiosk-12. Low numbers but high impact customers. I'll paste short list.

ops-bot: Suggestion: automate pin creation via DeployBot so ops can revert quickly.

mike: command sample: `/deploybot pin-tenant tenant-a tenant-b tenant-kiosk-12 --duration 24h --reason "post-cutover header quirk mitigation"`

courtney: I'm oncall during the window — I can monitor metrics and unpin if normalization patch lands successfully.

jen: rollback criteria proposal (publishable):
- sustained v2 5xx rate > 2% for >= 10 minutes OR
- client error rate (4xx/5xx from top 10 tenants) > 3x baseline for 5 minutes OR
- request routing mismatch metric (header-routing-mismatch) spikes > 10x baseline.

alex: add one more: tokenization mismatch / model output regressions alert (quality-monitor) if prompt failure rate increases > 2x.

mike: good. I'll add those to release notes and the ops checklist. Jen — if you can get a quick canary of the header normalization after 60 minutes, we can unpin early.

jen: will schedule a canary run at +1h after cutover and post results here. If canary is green (no routing mismatches for 15m) I'll signal to unpin.

deploybot: Pin command acknowledged — pins applied to tenant-a, tenant-b, tenant-kiosk-12 at 7401239890 by mike. Duration: 24h.

mike: Perfect. Courtney — please watch these dashboards first 2 hours: api-v2-5xx-rate, header-routing-mismatch, top-tenant-4xx, quality-monitor. Set temporary alert thresholds to the rollback criteria.

courtney: On it. I'll raise PagerDuty if any threshold breaches. :thumbsup:

mike: Alex / Jen / Sara — I'll follow up in the release notes doc with the exact wording and tenant list. Also adding a short migration note for customers: "If you see behavior that looks like you're still on v1 after the cutover, update SDK to latest or contact support; we may have temporarily pinned your tenant."

jen: I'll push the normalization canary config to edge-canary at +1h. If it fails, we'll keep pins and cutover remains conservative.

mike: thanks team. small but important: please mention the temporary pin thing prominently in the release email so CS doesn't get surprised.

deploybot: Note: to remove pin manually use `/deploybot unpin-tenant tenant-a` or wait for expiry.

mike: Closing — if no further objections I'll proceed with the pin command now and finish the release notes draft.

alex: no objections from infra.

sara: good with me.

courtney: 👍 monitoring ready.

mike: done. I'll ping again when normalization canary completes.
